questions.question: When was the rolling plan adopted?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**After the fifth five-year plan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Rolling Plan** was introduced after the termination of the **Fifth Five-Year Plan** in **1978** by the **Janata Party Government**.
 
• The concept of the Rolling Plan was aimed to replace the fixed five-year plans with a flexible annual plan that could be revised based on the country's economic performance and requirements.
 
• It was initiated under the leadership of **Morarji Desai**, who served as the Prime Minister of India during that period.
 
• This plan was designed to provide greater flexibility to policymaking, ensuring that the government could adapt to changing economic conditions without being constrained by the rigid framework of a fixed-term plan.
 
• The **Rolling Plan** was eventually abandoned, and the Sixth Five-Year Plan was introduced in **1980** under the Congress government led by **Indira Gandhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Five-Year Plans in India:**

 
 
• The concept of Five-Year Plans was introduced in India in **1951** inspired by the **Soviet Union's planning model**.
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan (1951-56)** focused on agricultural development and infrastructure building.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61)** emphasized industrialization and the development of heavy industries.
 
• Subsequent plans had specific objectives, such as poverty alleviation, employment generation, and sustainable growth.
 
 
 
• **Janata Party's Economic Policy:**
 
 
• The Janata Party, under **Morarji Desai's leadership**, sought to modify the planning process by introducing the Rolling Plan concept.
 
• This approach was designed to align economic priorities with the actual outcomes and adjust the policies dynamically.
 
• The government emphasized decentralization and reducing state control over industries and businesses during this period.
 
 
 
• **Challenges of Rolling Plan:**
 
 
• The Rolling Plan faced criticism for lacking long-term vision and consistency in policy-making.
 
• Frequent revisions led to confusion and inefficiencies in implementation.
 
• The Congress government, upon returning to power in **1980**, decided to revert to the traditional Five-Year Plan structure.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• During the late **1970s**, India was undergoing significant economic and political changes, including the Emergency period (1975-77).
 
• The Janata Party's policies reflected its commitment to democracy, decentralization, and liberalization of the economy.
 
• However, the lack of coherence and long-term planning under the Rolling Plan contributed to its failure.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Planning Commission:**

 
 
• Established in **1950**, the Planning Commission was responsible for creating and overseeing Five-Year Plans in India.
 
• It was replaced by the **NITI Aayog** in **2015** under the Modi government.
 
 
 
• **Sixth Five-Year Plan (1980-85):**
 
 
• This plan marked the return to fixed-term planning after the failure of the Rolling Plan.
 
• It focused on poverty alleviation, employment creation, and economic modernization.
 
• It was successful in achieving a growth rate of **5.7%**, which exceeded its target.
 
 
 
• **Flexible Planning:**
 
 
• While the Rolling Plan was abandoned, the idea of flexible planning influenced later approaches to economic policy-making in India.
 
• It highlighted the importance of adapting policies to changing circumstances and economic realities.

questions.question: Aligned with the objective of state control over vital sectors of the economy, the Industrial Policy of Resolution of 1956 was enacted, serving as the foundation for the ___________ Five Year Plan.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956** was a landmark policy document in India that aimed to strengthen the role of the state in controlling critical sectors of the economy. It emphasized the establishment of a socialist pattern of society by encouraging the public sector to play a dominant role.
 
• This resolution prioritized the allocation of resources to industries of strategic importance, such as defense, atomic energy, and heavy industries, under the direct control of the government.
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956-1961)**, formulated under the leadership of **Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru** and guided by economist **Dr. P.C. Mahalanobis**, was heavily influenced by the principles outlined in the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956.
 
• The Second Five-Year Plan focused on the development of capital goods industries, such as iron and steel, heavy engineering, and machine-building, aligning with the goal of state control over vital economic sectors.
 
• The resolution and the plan together aimed to create a balanced and self-reliant economy by prioritizing industrialization as a key driver of economic growth, poverty reduction, and modernization.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956:**

 
 
• The resolution divided industries into three categories:
 
 
• **Category 1:** Industries exclusively under state control, such as arms and ammunition, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• **Category 2:** Industries where the state would play a dominant role but private sector participation was allowed, including machine tools, fertilizers, and chemicals.
 
• **Category 3:** Industries left for private sector operation, with the state providing necessary support.
 
 
 
• The resolution aimed to reduce regional disparities by promoting industrial development in less developed regions.
 
• It emphasized the importance of small-scale industries to complement large-scale industries.
 
 
 
• **Second Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• It was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which emphasized heavy industries and capital goods production.
 
• The plan allocated substantial resources to the establishment of public sector enterprises like Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (**BHEL**) and Steel Authority of India (**SAIL**).
 
• This plan marked the beginning of planned industrial development with a focus on self-reliance.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of the Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The First Plan (1951-1956) focused on agriculture and irrigation to recover from the partition's aftermath.
 
• The Second Plan emphasized industrialization as a key tool for economic development.

• Bleaching powder is a white or light yellow powder with a strong chlorine smell.
 
• It is soluble in water, and its effectiveness depends on its chlorine content.
 
• Commonly used not only for swimming pools but also for disinfecting drinking water, cleaning surfaces, and bleaching fabrics.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Washing soda:** While washing soda (sodium carbonate) is used for cleaning purposes, it is not suitable for sanitizing water as it does not have disinfectant properties.

• It is a critical component in emergency relief efforts to purify water during natural disasters and public health crises.

• **Monitoring Pool Water:** Regular testing of chlorine levels and pH is essential to ensure the pool water remains safe and comfortable for swimmers.

questions.question: When trapped water in an aquifer is surrounded by layers of impermeable rock or clay, which apply positive pressure to the water, it is known as:
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• An **artesian aquifer** is a confined aquifer containing groundwater under positive pressure.
 
• It is surrounded by layers of **impermeable rock or clay** that prevent water from escaping, creating pressure.
 
• When water is tapped in an artesian aquifer, it rises above the top of the aquifer without the need for pumping, due to the **hydrostatic pressure**.
 
• This phenomenon occurs because the aquifer is sandwiched between impermeable layers and receives water from a higher elevation, allowing it to maintain positive pressure.
 
• Such aquifers are often used as a reliable source of groundwater for irrigation, municipal water supply, and industrial purposes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Unconfined Aquifer:**

 
 
• An unconfined aquifer is not bounded by impermeable layers, and the water table is exposed to atmospheric pressure.
 
• The water level in wells tapping this aquifer corresponds to the water table level, and pumping is required to extract water.
 
• These aquifers are susceptible to contamination from surface pollutants because of their open nature.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Aquifer:**
 
 
• The unsaturated zone, also known as the vadose zone, is located above the water table and contains both air and water within soil pores.
 
• It is not a reliable source of water extraction as it lacks saturation.
 
• This zone serves as a transit layer for water moving downward towards saturated aquifers.
 
 
 
• **Perched Aquifer:**
 
 
• A perched aquifer is formed above the main water table due to a localized impermeable layer (like clay) preventing water from draining downward.
 
• It is smaller and less reliable compared to other aquifer types.
 
• Such aquifers are often temporary and may disappear during dry periods.
 
 
 
• **Artesian Aquifer Characteristics:**
 
 
• These aquifers have **high pressure**, enabling water to flow to the surface naturally.
 
• They are commonly found in areas where water infiltrates at higher elevations and flows down to regions with impermeable rock layers.
 
• Examples include the Great Artesian Basin in **Australia**, one of the largest and most important artesian aquifers globally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Groundwater Recharge:**

 
 
• Artesian aquifers depend on recharge zones where water infiltrates from the surface, often at higher elevations.
 
• These recharge zones are critical for maintaining water pressure and ensuring long-term sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Artesian Aquifers:**
 
 
• They are extensively used for **irrigation**, drinking water supply, and industrial processes.
 
• Natural springs formed from artesian aquifers are often tourist attractions due to their scenic beauty and therapeutic properties.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Concerns:**
 
 
• Over-extraction of water from artesian aquifers can lead to a decrease in pressure and loss of natural spring flow.
 
• Proper management and regulation are essential to protect these resources from depletion and contamination.

questions.question: The Partition of Bengal was implemented by which British official?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Curzon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** was implemented by **Lord Curzon**, the then Viceroy of India, on **16 October 1905**.
 
• The partition was carried out with the objective of dividing Bengal into two provinces: **Eastern Bengal and Assam** and **Western Bengal**.
 
• It was officially justified by the British government on administrative grounds, citing Bengal's vast size and population as reasons for improved governance.
 
• The real motive behind the partition was to **weaken the nationalist movement** in Bengal by dividing the region along **religious lines**—Hindus in the west and Muslims in the east.
 
• The partition led to widespread protests and was eventually annulled in **1911** due to the strong opposition from Indian nationalists.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• Lord Curzon served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1899 to 1905**.
 
• He introduced several reforms, including the **Calcutta Corporation Act** and **Indian Universities Act**, but his tenure is most remembered for the controversial **Partition of Bengal**.
 
• He believed in strong imperial control and was criticized for his policies that favored British interests over Indian welfare.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Partition:**
 
 
• The partition led to the emergence of the **Swadeshi Movement**, which encouraged Indians to boycott British goods and promote indigenous industries.
 
• It united Indians across regions, religions, and communities, fostering a stronger sense of nationalism.
 
• While the British aimed to divide Hindus and Muslims, the partition inadvertently strengthened nationalist sentiments against colonial rule.
 
 
 
• **Protests and Annulment:**
 
 
• The partition faced significant opposition from leaders like **Rabindranath Tagore** and **Surendranath Banerjee**, who rallied people through protests, songs, and literature.
 
• On **12 December 1911**, the British government annulled the partition, citing administrative inefficiency and nationalist resistance.
 
• The capital of India was shifted from **Calcutta** to **Delhi** in the same year.
 
 
 
• **Religious Divide:**
 
 
• The partition exacerbated religious divisions between Hindus and Muslims, which later became a significant factor in India's struggle for independence.
 
• It laid the foundation for communal politics that continued to affect Indian society in the years leading up to partition in **1947**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other British Officials:**

 
 
• **Lord Minto:** Served as Viceroy of India from **1905 to 1910**. He is known for the **Morley-Minto Reforms (1909)**, which introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten:** The last Viceroy of India, oversaw India's independence and partition in **1947**.
 
• **Lord Wellesley:** Served as Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805**. He is known for implementing the **Subsidiary Alliance** system.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Partition of Bengal marked a turning point in India's struggle for independence, as it galvanized people to fight against British imperialism.
 
• It highlighted the British strategy of "divide and rule," which sought to weaken Indian unity.
 
• Understanding the partition is crucial to comprehending the socio-political dynamics that shaped India's journey to independence.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution instructs the State to ensure the right to work, education and public assistance in specific circumstances?

__
 
• **Article 41** of the Constitution of India falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV of the Constitution).
 
• It specifically instructs the State to make provisions for securing the **right to work, education, and public assistance** in cases of unemployment, old age, sickness, and disablement, and in other cases of undeserved want.
 
• Directive Principles are not enforceable by any court but are considered fundamental in the governance of the country.
 
• **Article 41** emphasizes the responsibility of the State to ensure social and economic justice to its citizens.
 
• The provisions under Article 41 aim to reduce inequalities and promote welfare measures for disadvantaged sections of society.

__

• DPSPs are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution under Articles 36 to 51.
 
• They are inspired by the **Irish Constitution** and are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts.
 
• The objective of DPSPs is to establish social and economic democracy and welfare in the country.
 
 
 
• **Article 38:**

• It was later amended by the **86th Constitutional Amendment Act of 2002**, which made elementary education a fundamental right under Article 21A.
 
 
 
• **Article 48:**
 
 
• It directs the State to organize agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines and to preserve and improve breeds and prohibit the slaughter of cows and calves.

• The **Directive Principles** act as guidelines for the government to frame laws and policies aimed at achieving socio-economic justice.
 
• Although not enforceable, they are fundamental for governance and the State is expected to apply them in its administration.
 
• The courts have upheld the importance of DPSPs in various judgments, stating that they are as significant as Fundamental Rights in guiding government policies.
 
• While **Article 41** specifically deals with the right to work, education, and public assistance, other articles like **39, 42, 43** complement it by addressing related issues like health, equal pay, and living wages.

questions.question: A can finish a work in 16 days, and B can do the same work in 12 days. While with the help of C, they completed the work in 4 days. in how many days can C alone do the same work?

Efficiency of C = 12 − (3 + 4) = 5 units/day.
